prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on your goals (social short vs. long-form, real-looking AI presenters vs. animated/text-driven), budget, languages, and how much manual editing you want to do. Below are top choices by use-case plus a short buying checklist and a recommendation request so I can pick the best fit for you.

Top picks (strength and one-line caveat)
- Synthesia — Best for AI human presenters and multilingual spokesperson videos. (Pro: very polished avatars and script-to-video; Con: relatively pricey and template-driven.)
- HeyGen — Strong alternative to Synthesia with competitive pricing and a wide avatar set. (Good if you want similar results for less.)
- D-ID — Best for talking-heads from photos and expressive reenactments. (Great for quick personalized ads using customer photos.)
- Runway — Best for generative and creative editing (text-to-video, inpainting, advanced effects). (Pro: powerful creative control; Con: steeper learning curve.)
- Canva / Clipchamp — Best for ease-of-use and fast social ads using templates + basic AI tools. (Great for teams that want speed and low cost.)
- Pictory — Best for turning long-form content (blogs/webinars) into short ads and social clips. (Automates summarization and captioning.)
- InVideo / Promo / Biteable — Best for template-based ad creation with strong libraries of footage and music. (Fast prebuilt formats for different platforms.)
- VEED / Kapwing — Best for collaborative browser editing with AI subtitles, auto-cuts, and branding tools. (Good mix of editing and AI helpers.)
- Runway/Adobe (for pros) — If you need advanced VFX or generative frames, use Runway or Adobe’s video tools with AI features. (For higher-end ads.)

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Platform/format: Instagram/Reels, TikTok, YouTube, display? (Some tools have prebuilt aspect ratios.)
- Style: AI human presenter, product demo, animated text + stock footage, or fully generated visuals?
- Script flow: Do you want script-to-video (just paste a script) or do you prefer manual editing?
- Languages/voices: Need multilingual voiceovers or captions?
- Budget & scale: One-off ad vs. many variants for A/B testing — enterprise tools help scale/adapt.
- IP & rights: confirm stock footage/music licensing and usage rights for ads.
- Output quality: 720/1080/4K? Social short vs. high-res pre-roll.

Recommended picks by common scenarios
- Quick TikTok/Reels ad with templates and captions: Canva, InVideo, Promo, or Pictory.
- Professional spokesperson ad (no actors): Synthesia or HeyGen.
- Personalized ads at scale (using customer names/photos): D-ID or Synthesia with personalization features.
- Repurposing webinars/blogs into multiple short ads: Pictory or Descript (Descript for audio+video editing).
- Highly creative/generative ad (novel visuals or advanced editing): Runway (or Adobe + plugins).
- Budget-conscious, collaborative editing: Clipchamp, VEED, or Kapwing.

A couple of practical notes
- Try free trials: most tools have free tiers or trials — test output quality, voice naturalness, and export limits.
- Test one ad on your channel before buying a big plan; measure CTR and retention, then iterate.
- If you need multi-variant ad production (many sizes/languages), prioritize platforms with bulk/templating features or API access.

If you tell me:
- platform (TikTok/Instagram/YouTube),
- style (real-person avatar, product shots, animated text),
- length (6–15s, 30s, 60s),
- and approximate budget,

I’ll recommend 1–2 specific tools and a short workflow to make the ad. (Note: my detailed knowledge goes up to June 2024; if you want I can quickly look up any recent changes or pricing for a particular tool.)
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
